text.p: World tanker organisation Intertanko said the detention of the 89,427 dwt tanker Nissos Amorgos by Venezuelan authorities following its grounding and oil spill in the Maracaibo Channel in February was unacceptable.
Intertanko, which represents 70 percent of the independent tanker fleet, said: "The detention is totally unnecessary and the amount being claimed quite unacceptable."
It said the Venezuelan authorities had prohibited the ship's master from leaving the country and demanded a bond of $46 million to cover claims, interest and other charges.

Intertanko managing director Dagfinn Lunde said Venezuela was a signatory to the two international conventions adopted by the International Maritime Organisation which cover liability and compensation for oil spills and should operate within them.
He said the Venezuelan authorities' actions "were now hampering the claims and payments process."
Around 25,000 barrels of oil were reported spilled when the Nissos Amorgos grounded on February 28.
Under the Civil Liability Convention, the ship owner and insurer are liable to pay compensation up to $7.2 million.

Lunde said a bank guarantee for this amount has been provided from a Venezuelan bank on behalf of the Gard P&I Club, the shipowner's insurers. He added that local indications were suggesting the spill clean-up would not exceed the $7.2 million provision.
For claims above $7.2 million, additional compensation up to $85 million is available from the International Oil Pollution Compensation Fund.
Intertanko said it understood a claims agency for the Nissos Amorgos incident has been established in Maracaibo by the IOPC and Gard to assist claimants.
Two other tankers have grounded in the Maracaibo Channel, through which 70 percent of Venezuela's oil exports pass, in the past six weeks despite compulsory pilotage.
Venezuela said a week ago that it would ask the United States, which built the Channel in 1928, for help to deepen it.
The Lake Maracaibo port captain has introduced a 36 foot draught restriction, down from a normal 39.5 feet.
Ship brokers say the draught reduction could cut Venezuela's oil exports by about 150,000 barrels per day.

Intertanko wants a wreck to be cleared from the channel which local maritime observers believe may have holed the Nissos Amorgos. Other local sources say tankers regularly touch bottom as they leave. --Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087
